Here is the commit message:
arm: dts: meson: Fix IRQ trigger type for macirq

A long running stress test on a custom board shipping an AXG SoCs and a
Realtek RTL8211F PHY revealed that after a few hours the connection
speed would drop drastically, from ~1000Mbps to ~3Mbps. At the same time
the 'macirq' (eth0) IRQ would stop being triggered at all and as
consequence the GMAC IRQs never ACKed.

After a painful investigation the problem seemed to be due to a wrong
defined IRQ type for the GMAC IRQ that should be LEVEL_HIGH instead of
EDGE_RISING.

The change in the macirq IRQ type also solved another long standing
issue affecting this SoC/PHY where EEE was causing the network
connection to die after stressing it with iperf3 (even though much
sooner). It's now possible to remove the 'eee-broken-1000t' quirk as
well.

Fixes: 9c15795a4f96 ("ARM: dts: meson8b-odroidc1: ethernet support")
Signed-off-by: Carlo Caione <ccaione@baylibre.com>
Reviewed-by: Martin Blumenstingl <martin.blumenstingl@googlemail.com>
Tested-by: Martin Blumenstingl <martin.blumenstingl@googlemail.com>
Signed-off-by: Kevin Hilman <khilman@baylibre.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a wrong definition of the IRQ trigger type for the GMAC IRQ, which was set to `EDGE_RISING` instead of `LEVEL_HIGH`. This incorrect configuration resulted in the 'macirq' not being triggered, leading to a drastic drop in connection speed and issues with the network stability under stress conditions. The situation was further compounded by the EEE feature causing network disconnection due to the IRQ not functioning as intended.

Here is the patch:
 			reg = <0xc9410000 0x10000
 			       0xc1108108 0x4>;
-			interrupts = <GIC_SPI 8 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING>;
+			interrupts = <GIC_SPI 8 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
 			interrupt-names = "macirq";
 			status = "disabled";

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
interrupts = <GIC_SPI 8 IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_RISING>;
```
Reason:
The IRQ trigger type for the GMAC was incorrectly set to `EDGE_RISING`, which means the IRQ would only be triggered on the rising edge of the signal. This designation can lead to missed interrupts under certain loads, resulting in the `macirq` not being triggered, causing network performance issues and instability during stress tests.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
interrupts = <GIC_SPI 8 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
```
Reason:
Changing the IRQ trigger type to `LEVEL_HIGH` means that the IRQ will be triggered continuously while the signal is high, ensuring that it remains active and preventing loss of interrupts. This correction stabilizes the network connection and resolves the issues related to the GMAC IRQ not being triggered under stress conditions.
